title: Marco Rubio Pushes US Energy Exports During Critical India Visit
author: Michael Chen
excerpt: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited India as both countries discuss expanding energy trade amid rising global oil disruptions linked to the Iran conflict.

title: Chick-fil-A Franchisee Sued by US Government Over Religious Discrimination
author: Emily Rodriguez
excerpt: The U.S. government has sued a Chick-fil-A franchise operator, alleging religious discrimination against an employee in a case that raises questions about workplace rights and accommodations.

title: Meta Platforms Settles First School District Lawsuit Over Youth Mental Health Crisis
author: Sarah Jenkins
excerpt: Meta settled the first US school district lawsuit over youth mental health harms allegedly linked to addictive social media platforms, marking a major legal milestone.

title: Toshifumi Suzuki Transformed 7-Eleven Into a Global Retail Giant
author: Robert Miller
excerpt: Toshifumi Suzuki, the businessman credited with building Japan’s 7-Eleven empire and revolutionizing global convenience retailing, died at age 93.

title: Nvidia Expands AI Infrastructure Partnerships in South Korea
author: Jessica Wu
excerpt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang unveils AI infrastructure deals with South Korea’s tech giants, including SK Telecom and SK Hynix, to build AI data centers, factories, and cloud computing networks, highlighting surging global demand for AI.

title: Allegiant and Sun Country Merger Reshapes Low-Cost Airline Industry
author: Sarah Jenkins
excerpt: Allegiant Air officially completed its acquisition of Sun Country Airlines, finalizing a $1.5 billion merger that creates one of the largest low-cost leisure airlines in the United States.

title: Trump Administration Launches Voluntary AI Testing Program for National Security Risks
author: Michael Chen
excerpt: President Donald Trump signed an executive order creating a voluntary framework for AI companies to submit advanced models for federal cybersecurity and national security reviews.

title: Dua Lipa Files $15 Million Lawsuit Against Samsung Over Unauthorized Image Use
author: Emily Rodriguez
excerpt: Pop singer Dua Lipa has filed a $15 million lawsuit against Samsung, accusing the tech giant of using her image on television packaging and promotional materials without authorization.
